body_markdown:
## Feature breakdown and usage limits by plan tier


As your output volume grows, Picsart scales its utility through a tiered credit and storage system. This forces a transition from casual content creation to structured asset management.


While the entry-level experience focuses on basic photo manipulation, the professional tiers introduce the resource overhead required to maintain a consistent brand identity across multiple social channels.


### AI credit allocations and refills


How many times a team can invoke generative tools like the AI Image Generator or AI Background Remover is determined by monthly allotments of AI credits.


On the Free plan, the minimal credit count acts as a trial. You can only test a handful of prompts before the tool locks until the next billing cycle.


By upgrading to the Pro or Ultra tiers, you increase these limits to hundreds or thousands of generations. This allows a social media manager to iterate on a single campaign visual dozens of times without exhausting the department's monthly budget.


Because credits don't roll over, any **unused balance is forfeited** at the end of the month. This necessitates a "use it or lose it" approach to content batching.


### Picsart cloud storage limits by plan


How many high-resolution projects a team can keep active and editable within the Picsart ecosystem simultaneously is dictated by cloud storage capacity.


0.1GB of storage is provided on the Free tier, which means users will likely run out of space almost immediately. This limits you to a few dozen compressed images before you must delete old work to start new projects.


100GB of storage is provided on the Pro tier, allowing for a significant library of high-resolution assets to be kept online, so users can maintain extensive project archives without needing local disk space.


This allows a small team to maintain a rolling archive of seasonal campaign assets without offloading files to external drives.


300GB of storage is provided on the Ultra tier, meaning power users can store extensive projects without needing to delete old files. This supports video-heavy workflows where raw clips and layered compositions would otherwise trigger "storage full" errors. High-resolution production remains uninterrupted by capacity constraints.


As your library of brand assets grows, this progression ensures the cost of the seat reflects the infrastructure required to host those files.


### Picsart watermark and commercial license rules


The shift from the Free plan to paid tiers is primarily a move from personal experimentation to legal commercial readiness.


Assets exported on the Free plan often carry a watermark or are restricted to personal use. They can't be used in a monetized YouTube video or a paid Instagram ad without risking a copyright strike.


> The shift from the Free plan to paid tiers is primarily a move from personal experimentation to legal commercial readiness.


Watermarks disappear and a commercial license is granted once you move to a Pro or Ultra subscription. This gives an agency the legal indemnity necessary to hand over final deliverables to a paying client.


To maximize ROI on these paid seats, you should use a tool like Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite to categorize and rename exported assets automatically. This makes licensed content easily searchable within the team’s shared folders.
